answer_channel_report.handle_identity_channel: 0 bits ACROSS units — handles are a per-unit permutation seeded from public coordinates only. Within a unit the schema discloses handle -> description, which is why membership carries the bound.
answer_channel_report.ordering_channel: 0 bits beyond membership — deliveries are re-sorted into canonical probe order, which is identical for every unit
answer_channel_report.rendering_channel: 0 bits — `legibility.assert_semantic_equivalence` hash-binds RAW and LEGIBLE to the same payload and rejects any locus term the raw form did not already contain

BLOCKER-01.finding: the corpus scenarios were built by injecting a NAMED fault, and the injected test's name survives into the public verifier stream as `test_corpus_scenario_<fault>`. On the primary population the marker appears in the model-visible initial context for 7 of 43 cases, and in the probe payloads (carried entirely by `rerun_verifier_isolated`) for 12 of 43. Every marker maps to exactly one true locus.
BLOCKER-01.mandatory_handling: marker presence is a MANDATORY STRATIFIER of the primary endpoint: R_correct must be reported separately for the marker-free and marker-bearing strata, and the pooled figure may not be reported alone
BLOCKER-01.measured: I(locus ; initial-context marker set) = 0.481 of 2.689 bits
BLOCKER-01.not_done: the corpus is NOT cleaned. Rewriting evidence to remove the markers would change the stimulus, invalidate comparability with the historical chain, and is a scientific change nobody authorized. It is declared per case instead.
BLOCKER-01.recorded_as: `construction_markers` and `answer_bearing_marker_present` on every case in the frozen binding
BLOCKER-01.title: injected-fault names are visible in the public failure evidence
BLOCKER-01.why_it_matters: the exposure is DIFFERENTIAL across arms. R0 sees 7 cases' markers; R3/R4 always deliver `rerun_verifier_isolated` and so see 12; R1/R2 see them only when the decoy draw includes that probe. C1 (R0 vs R1) therefore partly measures whether the model reads an injected fault name, not whether it revises a claim.

BLOCKER-02.finding: `leakage_bound` reports the consistency set as k = 3, i.e. 1.415 bits. But only 6 of the 8 probes are ever the discriminating one on this population — `rerun_verifier_isolated` and `inspect_verifier_config` never are — so an adversary who knows the policy discards decoys drawn from those two. The realized candidate set is |delivered n discriminating-capable|, which is 1 or 2 in the majority of unit-deliveries.
BLOCKER-02.measured: on the primary population at the frozen seed scope, over 43 cases x 2 repetitions: the candidate LOCUS set is size 1 in 4 of 86 deliveries, 2 in 28, 3 in 35, 4 in 19. Against a 2.807-bit prior (7 loci) the declared bound is 1.222 bits; realized leakage runs 0.807 to 2.807 bits, mean 1.395. In the 4 tail deliveries membership determines the locus outright — SINGLE's leak, which owner §6 excluded from the experiment.
BLOCKER-02.not_done: the intervention is NOT altered. Restricting decoys to discriminating-capable probes, or raising k, would change what R1/R2 deliver and therefore change C1 and C2. That is a scientific revision, not a repair.
BLOCKER-02.title: MASKED_K's realized membership leakage exceeds its declared bound

BLOCKER-03.finding: MASKED_K charges the full cost of the delivered set. With decoys drawn uniformly, the set can cost 9 against `max_payment = 7`, and the controller then delivers NOTHING rather than shrink the set (which would silently change the declared bound). The unit proceeds with no new evidence — behaviourally the R0 control.
BLOCKER-03.mandatory_handling: delivery success is a MANDATORY COVARIATE, and C1/C2 must report the delivery-failure rate per arm alongside the effect
BLOCKER-03.measured: 6 of 86 R1/R2 unit-deliveries (7.0%) on the primary population at the frozen seed scope. The rate is locus-correlated because the discriminating probe's cost varies by locus: declared_model fails 37.5% of the time (its discriminating probe, `validate_semantic_model`, costs 3), against 8.3% for authority, 7.1% for environment, 5.0% for implementation and 0% for evidence_collection, projection and verification_plan.
BLOCKER-03.not_done: neither the budget nor the decoy draw is changed. Owner §1 froze `max_payment = 7` and forbids raising it.
BLOCKER-03.title: MASKED_K delivery fails, locus-correlated, and collapses R1/R2 to R0
BLOCKER-03.why_it_matters: 'no evidence was delivered' is itself informative about the locus, and it dilutes C1 with units in which the treatment did not occur. An intention-to-treat analysis would understate the evidence effect; a per-protocol analysis would condition on a locus-correlated variable.

BLOCKER-04.finding: `unit_seed` takes the CONDITION NAME, so R1 and R2 seed different decoy draws and different handle permutations. Measured on the primary population at the frozen namespace: R1 and R2 receive DIFFERENT delivered evidence in 80 of 86 unit pairs (93.0%). R3 and R4 agree in 86 of 86, because FULL delivers everything and has no draw to diverge.
BLOCKER-04.the_fix_is_specified_not_applied: `DELIVERY_SEED_SCOPE` freezes the requirement — the seed key must be the legibility PAIR, not the arm. Applying it changes which decoys R1 receives, so it is left to owner adjudication rather than done here; nothing has run, so nothing is invalidated by deciding either way.
BLOCKER-04.title: R1 and R2 do not receive the same evidence, so C2 does not isolate rendering
BLOCKER-04.why_it_matters: owner §7 froze that R2 delivers exactly the evidence R1 delivers, and C2 is declared a PRIMARY comparison that isolates rendering. As implemented it varies rendering AND the evidence set at once, so C2 measures neither cleanly. `arm_difference_report` cannot see this: the two specs differ in exactly one DECLARED field, and the divergence lives in the seed, not in the spec.

masked_k_mechanism.handles: opaque per-unit handles carry no CROSS-unit semantics, but the action schema prints each handle's description, so within a unit the model can map handle -> probe. The defence is the delivered SET, not the handle.
masked_k_mechanism.ordering: delivery is re-sorted into canonical probe order, which is fixed across cases, so ordering adds nothing beyond membership
masked_k_mechanism.selection: the delivered set is the ONE evaluator-discriminating observation (from the sealed `acquisition-hidden-meta.json`) plus k-1 decoys drawn by `random.Random(seed)` where the seed is derived only from (experiment, namespace, case, arm, rep) — public run coordinates

masked_k_vs_single.both_are_evaluator_selected: MASKED_K's core observation is chosen using sealed evaluator metadata. Like SINGLE, it is MECHANISTIC / UPPER-BOUND and must never be read as deployable navigation or action-selection capability.
masked_k_vs_single.difference: SINGLE isolates the answer to one action; MASKED_K is a bounded-leak relaxation that hides it among k. They differ in the SIZE of the declared answer channel, not merely in wording, so substituting one for the other would change the experiment.

masked_k.delivered: the discriminating observation plus k-1 = 2 decoys

masked_k_vs_single.resolution: B — MASKED_K and SINGLE are scientifically DIFFERENT

masked_k_vs_single.which_belongs: MASKED_K. The authoritative frozen arms already say MASKED_K, and owner §6 forbids SINGLE as an arm. The prior owner-facing prose that said SINGLE was the error; the machine contract was right, and preserving MASKED_K rather than guessing was correct.

pilot_selection.not_tuned: the hash ordering fixes the walk before any coverage decision is made, so no case can be swapped in to make an arm look better; the resulting locus mix is an incidental consequence and is reported as unbalanced rather than presented as a sample
pilot_selection.purpose: PROTOCOL AND INSTRUMENT VALIDATION ONLY. The pilot is not an estimate of anything. It is not powered, it is not locus-balanced, and no scientific quantity may be reported from it.
pilot_selection.rule: 1. Start from the frozen primary population (43 gate-feasible determinate cases). 2. Order every case by sha256('evidence-revision-001|pilot-selection-v1|<case_id>'), ascending. The ordering key is a constant string and the case id — nothing tunable, nothing learned. 3. Walk that order and accept a case if and only if it introduces a value not yet covered on any coverage axis. 4. Stop at the first case where every axis is saturated.
